mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-40.9 to -34.3), indicating a steady restoration of discretionary out-of-home trips. Because transit use is a leading proxy for non-essential errand and leisure travel, continued transit recovery mechanically pulls RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -40.9 at t-3w to -34.3 at t-0w without reversal
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite TRANSIT continuing to rise for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has just crossed below the 8.0 level for the first time in the window (8.7, 8.7, 7.7, 7.3), meaning the share of time spent at home is shrinking. Crossing this threshold releases discretionary trips that had been suppressed, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks of the crossing.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.7 at t-3w to 7.3 at t-0w, first sub-8.0 reading
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the two weeks following the sub-8.0 RESIDENTIAL reading averages below the prior two-week average, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 8.0 without any RETAIL_REC gain.

mechanism_narrative: Routine restoration requires both a workplace-commute rebound and a grocery-trip normalization acting together: WORKPLACES improved from -42.0 to -32.0 while GROCERY_PHARM tightened from -7.0 to -2.4 in the same window. Only the joint movement signals genuine daily-routine recovery that spills into retail and recreation spending over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 10.0 points and GROCERY_PHARM rose 4.6 points between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: When both WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM improve together for two weeks, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days is not higher than the preceding 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS fell sharply from 38.0 at t-1w to 20.1 at t-0w, ending the outdoor-activity spike. Under a cooling-weather regime, leisure hours displaced from parks reallocate toward indoor commercial venues, so the parks decline is followed by a RETAIL_REC increase over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points from its four-week high
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 17.9 points from 38.0 at t-1w to 20.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Following a PARKS drop of more than 15 points from the four-week high, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days averages at or below its level in the 14 days before the drop.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has narrowed from -7.9 to -2.4, consistent with the lifting of essential-trip rationing or capacity caps. As grocery restrictions ease, the same policy loosening removes caps on retail and recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -3.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.5 points over the window and crossed above -3.0 at t-1w
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM exceeds -3.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The transit recovery is commute-driven, not discretionary: TRANSIT gained 6.6 points while RETAIL_REC stagnated and actually worsened from -23.9 to -25.3. When transit gains accrue without retail improvement for two consecutive weeks, the remaining transit recovery reflects mandatory work travel only, so RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC does not improve over the same two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 6.6 points from t-3w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell 1.6 points from t-1w to t-0w
regime_hint: partial reopening with work-only travel demand
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days by more than 2 points after a two-week TRANSIT-improves/RETAIL_REC-stalls divergence.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 7.0 in every week while WORKPLACES stays more than 30 points below baseline, the signature of a binding stay-at-home regime with active workplace restrictions. Under this regime, discretionary retail capacity stays suppressed and RETAIL_REC declines over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 7.0 and WORKPLACES below -30.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above 7.0 in all four weeks while WORKPLACES remained below -30.0
regime_hint: tightened containment with active workplace restrictions
failure_condition: With RESIDENTIAL above 7.0 and WORKPLACES below -30.0, RETAIL_REC one week later is higher than the current week's value.

mechanism_narrative: Leisure time is being redirected outdoors rather than to commercial venues: PARKS remains well above baseline (20.1) while RESIDENTIAL stays above 7.0, meaning non-work hours are split between home and open space. This substitution drains demand from indoor retail and recreation, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above 15.0 and RESIDENTIAL above 7.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged 27.5 and RESIDENTIAL averaged 8.1 across the four-week window
regime_hint: outdoor-substitution regime with suppressed indoor capacity
failure_condition: When PARKS exceeds 15.0 and RESIDENTIAL exceeds 7.0 simultaneously, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days averages above its level in the preceding 14 days.
